cmd_pnpm: Fast, disk space efficient package manager
cmd_add: Installs a package and any packages that it depends on. By default, any new package is installed as a prod dependency
cmd_audit: Checks for known security issues with the installed packages
cmd_bin: Print the directory where pnpm will install executables
cmd_catFile: Prints the contents of a file based on the hash value stored in the index file
cmd_catIndex: Prints the index file of a specific package from the store
cmd_config_set: Set the config key to the value provided
cmd_config_get: Print the config value for the provided key
cmd_config_delete: Remove the config key from the config file
cmd_create: Creates a project from a `create-*` starter kit
cmd_dedupe: Perform an install removing older dependencies in the lockfile if a newer version can be used
cmd_dlx: Run a package in a temporary environment
cmd_env_add: Installs the specified version(s) of Node.js without activating them as the current version
cmd_env_list: List Node.js versions available locally or remotely
cmd_env_remove: Removes the specified version(s) of Node.js
cmd_env_use: Installs the specified version of Node.js. The npm CLI bundled with the given Node.js version gets installed as well. This sets this version of Node.js as the current version
cmd_exec: Executes a shell command in scope of a project
cmd_fetch: Fetch packages from a lockfile into virtual store, package manifest is ignored
cmd_findHash: Experimental! Lists the packages that include the file with the specified hash
cmd_import: Generates pnpm-lock.yaml from an npm package-lock.json (or npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock) file
cmd_install: Install all dependencies for a project
cmd_installTest: Runs a `pnpm install` followed immediately by a `pnpm test`. It takes exactly the same arguments as `pnpm install`
cmd_licenses_list: Check the licenses of the installed packages
cmd_link: Connect the local project to another one
cmd_list: Print all the versions of packages that are installed, as well as their dependencies, in a tree-structure
cmd_pack: Create a tarball from a package
cmd_patchCommit: Generate a patch out of a directory
cmd_publish: Publishes a package to the registry
cmd_recursive: Concurrently performs some actions in all subdirectories with a `package.json` (excluding node_modules). A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file may be used to control what directories are searched for packages
cmd_remove: Removes packages from `node_modules` and from the project's `package.json`
cmd_server_start: Starts a service that does all interactions with the store. Other commands will delegate any store-related tasks to this service
cmd_server_status: Prints information about the running server
cmd_start: Runs an arbitrary command specified in the package's "start" property of its "scripts" object
cmd_store: Reads and performs actions on pnpm store that is on the current filesystem
cmd_store_add: Adds new packages to the pnpm store directly. Does not modify any projects or files outside the store
cmd_store_path: Returns the path to the active store directory
cmd_store_prune: Removes unreferenced (extraneous, orphan) packages from the store. Pruning the store is not harmful, but might slow down future installations
cmd_store_status: Checks for modified packages in the store. Returns exit code 0 if the content of the package is the same as it was at the time of unpacking
cmd_test: Runs a package's "test" script, if one was provided
cmd_unlink: Removes the link created by `pnpm link` and reinstalls package if it is saved in `package.json`
cmd_update: Updates packages to their latest version based on the specified range. You can use "*" in package name to update all packages with the same pattern
cmd_why: Shows the packages that depend on <pkg>
opt_color: Controls colors in the output. By default, output is always colored when it goes directly to a terminal
opt_loglevel: What level of logs to report. Any logs at or higher than the given level will be shown. Levels (lowest to highest): debug, info, warn, error. Or use "--silent" to turn off all logging
opt_stream: Stream output from child processes immediately, prefixed with the originating package directory. This allows output from different packages to be interleaved
opt_aggregateOutput: Aggregate output from child processes that are run in parallel, and only print output when child process is finished. It makes reading large logs after running `pnpm recursive` with `--parallel` or with `--workspace-concurrency` much easier (especially on CI). Only `--reporter=append-only` is supported
opt_workspaceRoot: Run the command on the root workspace project
opt_recursive: Run the command for each project in the workspace
opt_globalDir: Specify a custom directory to store global packages
opt_storeDir: The directory in which all the packages are saved on the disk
opt_virtualStoreDir: The directory with links to the store (default is node_modules/.pnpm). All direct and indirect dependencies of the project are linked into this directory
opt_offline: Trigger an error if any required dependencies are not available in local store
opt_preferOffline: Skip staleness checks for cached data, but request missing data from the server
opt_saveProd: Save package to your `dependencies`. The default behavior
opt_saveWorkspaceProtocol: Save packages from the workspace with a "workspace:" protocol. True by default
opt_configDep: Save the dependency to configurational dependencies
opt_saveCatalog: Save package to the default catalog
opt_saveCatalogName: Save package to the specified catalog
opt_workspace: Only adds the new dependency if it is found in the workspace
opt_allowBuild: A list of package names that are allowed to run postinstall scripts during installation
opt_frozenLockfile: Don't generate a lockfile and fail if an update is needed. This setting is on by default in CI environments, so use --no-frozen-lockfile if you need to disable it for some reason
opt_force: Force reinstall dependencies: refetch packages modified in store, recreate a lockfile and/or modules directory created by a non-compatible version of pnpm. Install all optionalDependencies even they don't satisfy the current environment(cpu, os, arch)
opt_lockfileOnly: Dependencies are not downloaded. Only `pnpm-lock.yaml` is updated
opt_reporter: The output is always appended to the end. No cursor manipulations are performed
opt_silent: No output is logged to the console, not even fatal errors
opt_auditLevel: Only print advisories with severity greater than or equal to one of the following: low|moderate|high|critical. Default: low
opt_auditFix: Add overrides to the package.json file in order to force non-vulnerable versions of the dependencies
opt_ignoreRegistryErrors: Use exit code 0 if the registry responds with an error. Useful when audit checks are used in CI. A build should fail because the registry has issues
opt_ignoreUnfixable: Ignore all CVEs with no resolution
opt_parseable: Show parseable output instead of tree view
opt_depth: Max display depth of the dependency tree
opt_location: When set to "project", the .npmrc file at the nearest package.json will be used. If no .npmrc file is present in the directory, the setting will be written to a pnpm-workspace.yaml file
opt_dedupeCheck: Check if running dedupe would result in changes without installing packages or editing the lockfile. Exits with a non-zero status code if changes are possible
opt_dlxPackage: The package to install before running the command
opt_shellMode: Runs the script inside of a shell. Uses /bin/sh on UNIX and \cmd.exe on Windows
opt_remote: List the remote versions of Node.js
opt_verifyStoreIntegrity: If false, doesn't check whether packages in the store were mutated
opt_childConcurrency: Controls the number of child processes run parallelly to build node modules
opt_hoistPattern: Hoist all dependencies matching the pattern to `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`. The default pattern is * and matches everything. Hoisted packages can be required by any dependencies, so it is an emulation of a flat node_modules
opt_ignoreWorkspace: Ignore pnpm-workspace.yaml if exists in the parent directory, and treat the installation as normal non-workspace installation
opt_lockfileDir: The directory in which the pnpm-lock.yaml of the package will be created. Several projects may share a single lockfile
opt_mergeGitBranchLockfiles: Merge lockfiles were generated on git branch
opt_modulesDir: The directory in which dependencies will be installed (instead of node_modules)
opt_networkConcurrency: Maximum number of concurrent network requests
opt_noHoist: Dependencies inside the modules directory will have access only to their listed dependencies
opt_noLockfile: Don't read or generate a `pnpm-lock.yaml` file
opt_optimisticRepeatInstall: Skip reinstall if the workspace state is up-to-date
opt_packageImportMethod: Clones/hardlinks or copies packages. The selected method depends from the file system
opt_preferFrozenLockfile: If the available `pnpm-lock.yaml` satisfies the `package.json` then perform a headless installation
opt_publicHoistPattern: Hoist all dependencies matching the pattern to the root of the modules directory
opt_resolutionOnly: Re-runs resolution: useful for printing out peer dependency issues
opt_shamefullyHoist: All the subdeps will be hoisted into the root node_modules. Your code will have access to them
opt_sideEffectsCache: Use or cache the results of (pre/post)install hooks
opt_sideEffectsCacheReadonly: Only use the side effects cache if present, do not create it for new packages
opt_strictPeerDependencies: Fail on missing or invalid peer dependencies
opt_useRunningStoreServer: Only allows installation with a store server. If no store server is running, installation will fail
opt_useStoreServer: Starts a store server in the background. The store server will keep running after installation is done. To stop the store server, run `pnpm server stop`
opt_onlyProjects: Display only dependencies that are also projects within the workspace
opt_compatible: Print only versions that satisfy specs in package.json
opt_outdatedFormat: Prints the outdated dependencies in the given format. Default is "table". Supported options: "table, list, json"
opt_noTable: Prints the outdated packages in a list. Good for small consoles
opt_sortBy: Specify the sorting method. Currently only `name` is supported
opt_out: Customizes the output path for the tarball. Use `%s` and `%v` to include the package name and version, e.g., `%s.tgz` or `some-dir/%s-%v.tgz`. By default, the tarball is saved in the current working directory with the name `<package-name>-<version>.tgz`
opt_packDestination: Directory in which `pnpm pack` will save tarballs. The default is the current working directory
opt_workspaceConcurrency: Set the maximum number of concurrency. Default is 4. For unlimited concurrency use Infinity
opt_editDir: The package that needs to be modified will be extracted to this directory
opt_ignoreExisting: Ignore existing patch files when patching
opt_patchesDir: The generated patch file will be saved to this directory
opt_access: Tells the registry whether this package should be published as public or restricted
opt_dryRun: Does everything a publish would do except actually publishing to the registry
opt_noGitChecks: Don't check if current branch is your publish branch, clean, and up to date
opt_otp: When publishing packages that require two-factor authentication, this option can specify a one-time password
opt_publishBranch: Sets branch name to publish. Default is master
opt_reportSummary: Save the execution results of every package to "pnpm-exec-summary.json". Useful to inspect the execution time and status of each package
opt_tag: Registers the published package with the given tag. By default, the "latest" tag is used
opt_pending: Rebuild packages that were not build during installation. Packages are not build when installing with the --ignore-scripts flag
opt_includeWorkspaceRoot: When executing commands recursively in a workspace, execute them on the root workspace project as well
opt_linkWorkspacePackages: Locally available packages are linked to node_modules instead of being downloaded from the registry. Convenient to use in a multi-package repository
opt_noBail: Continues executing other tasks even if a task threw an error
opt_reverse: Reverse the order that packages get ordered in. Disabled by default
opt_sharedWorkspaceLockfile: Creates a single pnpm-lock.yaml file in the root of the workspace. A shared lockfile also means that all dependencies of all projects will be in a single node_modules
opt_sort: Sort packages topologically (dependencies before dependents). Pass --no-sort to disable
opt_ifPresent: Avoid exiting with a non-zero exit code when the script is undefined
opt_runParallel: Completely disregard concurrency and topological sorting, running a given script immediately in all matching packages with prefixed streaming output. This is the preferred flag for long-running processes such as watch run over many packages
opt_reporterHidePrefix: Hide project name prefix from output of running scripts. Useful when running in CI like GitHub Actions and the output from a script may create an annotation
opt_sequential: Run the specified scripts one by one
opt_background: Runs the server in the background
opt_ignoreStopRequests: Disallows stopping the server using `pnpm server stop`
opt_ignoreUploadRequests: Disallows creating new side effect cache during install
opt_port: The port number to use, when TCP is used for communication
opt_protocol: The communication protocol used by the server
opt_setupForce: Override the PNPM_HOME env variable in case it already exists
opt_interactive: Show outdated dependencies and select which ones to update
opt_updateDepth: How deep should levels of dependencies be inspected. Infinity is default. 0 would mean top-level dependencies only
opt_changedFilesIgnorePattern: Defines files to ignore when filtering for changed projects since the specified commit/branch
opt_failIfNoMatch: If no projects are matched by the command, exit with exit code 1 (fail)
opt_filter: Restricts the scope to package names matching the given pattern. E.g.: foo, "@bar/*"
opt_filterProd: Restricts the scope to package names matching the given pattern similar to --filter, but it ignores devDependencies when searching for dependencies and dependents
opt_testPattern: Defines files related to tests. Useful with the changed since filter. When selecting only changed packages and their dependent packages, the dependent packages will be ignored in case a package has changes only in tests
